images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: environment art direction reference for ArchaeologyGame, a PC fossil preparation game; NOT a screenshot, original museum interior design.
Primary request: a convincing, beautiful small natural history museum gallery in polished stylized 3D. A warm illustration brought to life, inviting and carefully curated, the cozy museum feeling of Animal Crossing but with more natural tactile materials and scientific credibility. This should be a feasible real-time 3D scene to recreate in Godot with individual modeled assets, NOT a photorealistic architectural visualization.
Scene: one intimate gallery bay, warm honey-walnut wood wainscoting with crafted profiles and bevels, cream plaster arches, a tall arched window admitting soft neutral daylight, muted bottle-green recessed display niches, aged brass fixtures, stone floor with restrained geometric inlay. A quiet older natural history museum, cared for, not dilapidated. Small background glazed specimen cabinet, one antique framed geological illustration, discreet wall lamps, a fern near the window. Compose a real room with depth and elegant proportions, neither cavernous nor cluttered.
Main subjects: TWO player's prepared fossil blocks still inside their irregular earth-and-stone matrix, prominently displayed in the foreground. A longer wide ochre-brown rock slab bearing a small theropod skeleton in ivory bone relief, lying on its side in the original fossil bed, skull, ribs, spine and limbs visible, resting on an inclined low walnut display stand with subtly rounded corners, slender supports and dark recessed bed. Beside it, smaller distinct rounded grey-beige matrix block containing an ivory ribbed ammonite in strong 3D relief, on its own compact complementary pedestal. The rock blocks have credible irregular thick edges, partial earth remnants, sculpted depth, raised fossils, no rigid rectangular rock cuts. Separate tiny ivory museum labels on brass holders do not obstruct the pieces. The fossils must remain the first thing the eye reads. No upright mounted dinosaur skeleton.
Composition: one widescreen 16:9 image, elevated three-quarter frontal view into the gallery bay, near-orthographic perspective, gently looking down enough to clearly read both inclined fossil blocks. Primary displays occupy lower middle half; architecture frames them. Clean foreground camera sightlines for moving smoothly from one exhibit to the neighboring exhibit, no people or avatar. Modest usable floor space, a neighboring gallery hinted through one arch.
Materials/style: confidently modeled bevels, gently softened edges, readable larger forms, subtle painterly texture variation. Rich but restrained wood grain, matte stone and plaster, subdued brass, warm ivory fossils contrasted against earthy matrices. Smooth natural shapes without conspicuous low-poly facets; mature cozy art, no toy plastic.
Lighting: balanced cool-neutral window fill plus warm museum lamps on fossil relief, soft grounded contact shadows, realistic depth, gentle tonal hierarchy. Bright and welcoming enough to read materials; preserve ivory detail, no orange wash, no blown highlights, no cinematic haze.
Constraints: no HUD, no game UI, no large green text boards, no captions, no watermark, no recognizable existing game assets or characters, no decorative fantasy props. Small labels can be blank. Deliver a single high-quality original art-direction image, not a moodboard, not multiple panels.

Use case: style-transfer. Edit this museum concept, retaining the same room composition, the two foreground inclined fossil-in-matrix displays, arched window, niches, wood cabinet, framing and overall warm palette. Change ONLY the artistic rendering and material/detail treatment to a distinctly polished stylized 3D cozy game art target, closer to the appealing readability of Animal Crossing's museum, not realistic archviz.
The current image is too photographic. Make the visible change substantial: softly exaggerated broad architectural proportions, clear sculpted shapes, rounded modeled bevels, appealing chunky furniture profiles, simplified hand-painted texture gradients and sparse wood grain, matte surfaces. Flatten tiny photographic noise and ornament into clear medium-scale forms. Floor must be matte stone, not glossy marble; no reflected window or mirror highlights. Bone ivory with simplified sculptural ridges, earth/stone broad tactile facets and curated texture, no micro photogrammetry. Vegetation simplified stylized leaf clusters. Brass has restrained broad highlights, glass very subtle. Keep believable depth, warm diffuse lighting, neutral daylight, grounded soft shadows and modeling sophistication; not a flat 2D cartoon, not voxel or conspicuous low-poly, not childish toy plastic.
The player specimens remain physically in their irregular rock blocks, framed as the focus, not extracted or upright skeletons. Preserve the natural history museum identity and original architecture. No people, UI, captions, logos or readable lettering. One widescreen 16:9 scene. This is a concept art target, not actual game rendering.
